shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Current inventory is 1 each of C, A, B - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. I'd rather keep balanced holdings or trade a good I have surplus of.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of C, A, and B. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 0 B and 2 A, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.
Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, creating a worse imbalance since I value variety. Not beneficial.
Current inventory is balanced at 1 each. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Not beneficial.

Current inventory is balanced (1C,1A,1B). Trading 1B for 1C would make it 2C,1A,0B, reducing variety and lowering utility since I'd go from having one of each to having zero of a good. Not beneficial given my preference for variety.

This trade would leave me with C:3, A:1, B:0, which is highly unbalanced (I'd have zero B and excess C). Since I value variety, this reduces my utility rather than improving it. I'd rather keep a more even distribution.

Trading 1 A for 1 B would just swap which good I have 1 of to 0, leaving me with 2 B and 0 A - reducing variety instead of increasing it. Current holdings are already balanced (1 each), so this trade would make my bundle less diverse, not more.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of C, A, B. Trading away B for A would just swap which good I have less of, resulting in 0 B and 2 A, reducing variety and not improving my utility. I prefer to keep balanced holdings or trade to increase variety, not decrease it.

Current inventory is 1 C, 1 A, 1 B - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 1 C, 3 A, 0 B, which is highly unbalanced and reduces variety value. I prefer to keep an even spread across goods.

Trading my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety instead of improving it. Since I value equal distribution and currently have 1 of each good, this trade would harm my utility.

Current inventory is C:1, A:1, B:1 - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for another C would make me have C:2, A:1, B:0, which reduces variety and lowers my utility since I'd have zero of one good.
Current inventory is balanced at 1 each. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 3 C, 1 A, 0 B - a very unbalanced bundle that reduces variety, which I value. Not beneficial.

I currently have 3 A and 0 B and 0 C, so my inventory is heavily skewed toward A. Trading 1 A for 1 B increases variety, moving me toward a more balanced bundle (2A, 1B), which increases my utility given my preference for diversity.
Giving up 2 A for just 1 B would leave me with only 1 A and 1 B, over-concentrating my loss in A. A fairer 1-for-1 trade would improve variety without sacrificing too much value.

Currently I have 2C, 1A, 0B - very imbalanced. Trading away 1A (going to 0) for 1B (going to 1) gives me 2C, 0A, 1B, which is still imbalanced but at least I get a good I have none of. Actually let's check: after trade I'd have C:2, A:0, B:1. That's same variety issue but now missing A instead of B. Not clearly better. However since I value B at zero currently, gaining first unit of B has high marginal value, while losing my only A drops me to zero there too. Since both are symmetric in scarcity, but I gain a good I have none of (B) at cost of a good I already have only 1 of (A), net variety stays same. Still, having C:2,A:0,B:1 vs C:2,A:1,B:0 - both have one good at 0. Utility roughly equal, slight preference to accept to diversify away from redundant C-heavy trend and test market. Accepting since it maintains balance and opens door to further trades for A back later.

Currently I have 2 C, 1 A, 0 B - a very unbalanced bundle. Trading 1 C (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward a more even distribution: 1 C, 1 A, 1 B, increasing my utility given my preference for variety.
Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with 0C, 1A, 1B - trading away my entire C stock is too costly. I'd rather trade 1C for 1B to diversify while keeping some C.

Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety instead of improving it. Since I already have equal amounts (1 each), this trade would create imbalance rather than help.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of C, A, B. Trading away my B for another A would give me 2A, 0B, 1C - reducing variety and making B scarce for me. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility, not increase it.

Current inventory is C:1, A:1, B:1 - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with C:1, A:3, B:0, creating a worse imbalance since I'd have zero of B and excess A. Since I value variety, this reduces my utility despite gaining more total goods.

Trading away my only C for a second B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 2 B — reducing variety and losing my only unit of a good. Since I value variety, this decreases my utility rather than increasing it.
Current inventory is C:1, A:1, B:1 - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with C:2, A:1, B:0, reducing variety and thus utility since I'd have zero of one good.

Current inventory is 1C/1A/1B, a balanced set. Trading away my only B for 2C would leave me with 3C/1A/0B, creating a highly imbalanced bundle since I value variety. This decreases my utility despite the numerical gain in goods.
I currently have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - a perfectly even distribution across all three goods, which maximizes value given my preference for variety.

Giving up both A would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, trading a good I have 2 of for one I have 0 of, but going to zero A is too extreme - I'd rather trade only 1 A for 1 B to balance my inventory (C:1, A:1, B:1) instead of ending up with (C:1, A:0, B:1). This exact trade over-concentrates by leaving me with no A at all.

I currently have only 1 C, so giving it away would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, worsening variety rather than improving it. My inventory is C:1, A:2, B:0 - trading my only C for B just swaps which good I'm missing, not a net gain. I'd rather trade an A (which I have 2 of) for B to improve variety while keeping C.

Current inventory has 0 A and 1 B, 1 C. Trading B for A would give me C:1, A:1, B:0 - same total variety spread, but since I currently have 0 A (a good I completely lack), gaining it is more valuable than keeping a second unit of B I already have. This improves balance toward equal variety.
Giving up my only B would leave me with 0 B, 2 A, 1 C - trading one scarcity for another. I'd rather get 1 A for the B, keeping a more balanced bundle. Rejecting to negotiate a better ratio.

Trading my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety (I'd have A:0, B:2, C:0). Since I value variety, this worsens my bundle - I'd rather keep C and seek A instead. Current C:1,B:1 is balanced; giving up C for B creates imbalance without gaining a new good type.

This trade would give me 2×C and 0×B, making my bundle less diverse (I'd have no A or B). Since I value variety, trading my only B for another C when I already have equal C doesn't improve my utility - it would leave me with 2C, 0A, 0B instead of a more balanced 1C, 0A, 1B. I'd rather acquire A to diversify, or keep my current balance.

This trade would leave me with C:3, A:0, B:0, which is highly imbalanced and eliminates my only B good entirely. I value variety, so trading away my only B for more C (which I already have most of) reduces my utility. I'd rather seek a trade that gets me A while keeping some B.
Currently I have 0 B and 2 A, so trading 1 A for 1 B moves me toward a more balanced inventory (C:1, A:1, B:1), which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with C:1, A:0, B:1 - eliminating a good entirely, which hurts variety. A better trade would be 1A for 1B to balance my inventory to C:1, A:1, B:1, maximizing variety.

Current inventory: C:1, A:2, B:0. Giving away my only C for B would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just swapping which good I lack instead of gaining variety. Since I value variety, I'd rather keep C and acquire B without giving up my sole unit of C, or negotiate a trade using A (which I have more of) instead.

I currently have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B — a very uneven distribution. Trading away 1 A (which I have surplus of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward a balanced 1-1-1 bundle, increasing my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up both my A for just 1 B would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, going from a balanced but variety-poor bundle (C1,A2,B0) to an even more skewed one (C1,A0,B1). I'd rather trade only 1 A for 1 B to gain variety while keeping some A.

Trading my only C (currently my scarcest good along with B=0) for B would leave me with C:0, A:2, B:1 - still uneven and I'd lose my only unit of C entirely. Better to keep some C and try to get B without fully depleting C, or negotiate a better ratio.

Current inventory is 1C, 2A, 0B - heavily skewed with no B at all. Trading 1A (which I have 2 of) for 1B (which I have none of) moves me toward a more balanced 1C/1A/1B bundle, increasing utility since I value variety.
Giving up both my A for only 1 B would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, trading a balanced holding for an even more skewed one. I'd rather trade only 1 A for 1 B to diversify into C=1, A=1, B=1.

Trading away my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting scarcity rather than improving variety. Current bundle is C:1, A:2, B:0 - giving up my sole C unit for B would make me have zero of C, which is equally bad for variety. I'd rather keep C and acquire B without depleting C entirely, or negotiate a trade that doesn't zero out any good."
